claims.text: The library runs on PostgreSQL with pgvector on spark: documents, repo documents, full text and vectors live in one self-hosted database with a real vector index, API and MCP clients see no contract change, and retrieval quality is re-baselined at cutover
API and MCP clients see no contract change: the HTTP routes, MCP tools and /api/status shape stay as they are; only the storage under them moves
Sibling clients (culture-rules, Gwen, xteink) keep using the HTTP API on 127.0.0.1:8796 with their API keys; nothing outside the library reads the database
Item and repo-doc file bytes stay on the filesystem under data/files/<aa>/<sha256>, and the private S3 mirror (outbox, worker, bucket) keeps working unchanged
Embedding and reranking stay on the local lobes gateway (gemma2-embed, reranker); no document text goes to a third-party service, so MongoDB-style automated embedding via a cloud API is out
The xteink migration keeps reading its source database with sqlite3; only its destination lookup moves to the new store
Documents, repo documents, full text, vectors and every other library table live in one self-hosted PostgreSQL database with the pgvector extension, run as a service in the spark compose stack
Vectors are stored as pgvector vector(768) with an HNSW index, and the in-process vector cache, vector_log table and its triggers are removed

hard_questions.text: Does core/ keep SQLite as a second backend behind a storage interface (for tests, offline use and the zero-dependency rule), or does the library become Postgres-only?

claims.text: Full-text search is reimplemented on Postgres: title weighted above body, English stemming, prefix match on the last term, and highlighted snippets, for items and repo docs separately

Search scores and rankings change at cutover; stored eval sets stay valid because they are anchored by chunk text sha, and the baseline (sets 1-8, rerank on and off) is re-run on Postgres as the new comparison point

hard_questions.text: Full-text ranking: accept Postgres ts_rank (simpler, rankings move), or add a BM25 extension so ranking stays close to today's bm25?

claims.text: The push transaction stays atomic in Postgres: a repo-doc version or draft, its feed event and its mirror outbox row commit together on one connection, as do tombstones
SQLite-only locking workarounds get Postgres equivalents: the unlink-after-commit of unreferenced blobs, and API-key last_used stamping that never waits on a writer

SQLite-specific SQL is ported in every core module: AUTOINCREMENT + lastrowid become identity + RETURNING, integer booleans become boolean, MAX(a,b) becomes GREATEST, json_extract on TEXT becomes jsonb, INSERT OR REPLACE/IGNORE become ON CONFLICT, the feed column named cursor is quoted or renamed, and ? placeholders change
Schema changes run through a one-time, versioned migration runner instead of DDL and migrations re-applied on every open

The live data moves once from SQLite to Postgres with ids, cursors and counts preserved: items, repo docs and their versions and drafts, feed, API keys, eval sets and runs, sources, projects, spec links, mirror outbox and the vectors

hard_questions.text: Cutover style: a one-shot migration during a short write freeze with the SQLite backup and image as rollback, or a period where both stores run side by side?

claims.text: Backup and restore are rebuilt on pg_dump/pg_restore plus the existing verified blob copy and manifest, with a restore drill before cutover
deploy restart starts and checks the Postgres service too, and the database password comes from grant like every other secret, never from live.env

hard_questions.text: Postgres version and image: which major version and pgvector build, and does the library connect with psycopg 3 (the code is synchronous)?

claims.text: Tests run against Postgres in CI and locally, with an isolated database or schema per xdist worker, and the SQLite-coupled tests are rewritten
Runbooks and agent docs describe the Postgres stack: deploy.md (what runs, backups, restart, schema upgrades, rollback), backup.md, and CLAUDE.md and its sibling harness files

open_vagueness.text: How well HNSW recall holds under our filters (private/public, owner, kind, item ids) at low selectivity, since pgvector filters after the index scan; measure with the eval harness after the port
Whether the spark stack has the RAM and disk headroom for Postgres plus an HNSW index over about 70k (and growing) 768-dimension vectors next to the current services

scope_entries.finding: The written API contracts (repodocs.md, eval.md) never mention SQLite; MCP parity tests compare tool names to the HTTP routes; /api/status exposes counts, index, retrieval and mirror blocks but no db path or WAL setting. routes_status.py runs raw COUNT/MAX/COALESCE SQL that must keep its output shape
Only the library reads library.db; siblings call the HTTP API with scoped keys. The one other sqlite3 reader is the xteink import, which reads xteink's own old database

The DB holds only metadata (sha256, size, format); bytes are written atomically to data/files before the DB insert. The S3 mirror is the only existing storage abstraction (S3Backend). Postgres replaces the metadata store only; the data volume stays

scope_entries.surface: culture_library/gateway.py:33; repodoc privacy decision c31; MongoDB automated-embedding docs
scope_entries.finding: Embeddings come from the gateway with Retrieval-document/Retrieval-query prompts. All repo docs are private. Postgres only stores and indexes vectors the library already computes
xteink.py opens the old xteink library.db read-only with sqlite3 (a legacy source format) and looks up the destination by the library.db path, which must ask the Postgres store instead

Compose has library, mcp and cloudflared and one data volume; a postgres service (pgvector image), its own volume and a pg_isready healthcheck are new. library needs depends_on service_healthy. The Dockerfile installs .[server,s3]; a Postgres driver extra joins it

Vectors are float32 BLOBs (pack_vec) with a model column, scored by brute force in Python with the 0.19.8 cache. The live dimension is 768 (gemma2-embed), measured on spark; 7,855 item and 61,932 repo-doc chunks. Search scores mixed-model rows together today

FTS5 tables search_fts and repodoc_fts use porter unicode61, bm25 weights 5.0 (title) and 1.0 (body), snippet() with [ ] markers and 12 tokens, and quoted AND terms with a * prefix on the last. Postgres has tsvector setweight + ts_rank/ts_headline, which do not reproduce bm25

Eval samples anchor on sha256 of the chunk text, so sets survive; runs store retrieved shas and ID metrics, never raw bm25 scores. c47 (baseline must not move) cannot hold through an FTS engine change and must be re-argued. Several tests pin exact scores

RepoDocs.push runs under one store.connect() and calls on_write(conn, result) inside it (d6), where the route appends the feed event and enqueues the mirror. Cross-module atomicity of version + feed + outbox is the invariant to keep

library._unlink_unreferenced relies on SQLite's single writer lock; keys._stamp_last_used opens a raw sqlite3 connection with a 100 ms busy_timeout and string-matches 'no such table'. Both need advisory locks or lock_timeout/SKIP LOCKED style equivalents

scope_entries.surface: core/repodocs.py, feed.py, keys.py, eval_store.py, library.py, mirror.py, uploaders.py, projects.py, speclinks.py, sources.py
scope_entries.finding: AUTOINCREMENT in 6 modules with cur.lastrowid; bare INTEGER booleans (on_default_branch, private, running); scalar MAX() in repodocs; json_extract in library.py:71,539; INSERT OR REPLACE in eval_store:312; feed.cursor is a Postgres reserved word; uploaders.visible_sql splices ? fragments into other modules' SQL; library._sha_tables introspects sqlite_master

scope_entries.surface: core/store.py:165-174,201-247; core/mirror.py:48-73; triggers in indexer.py:115 and vector_cache.py:51
scope_entries.finding: register_schema fragments are split on ';' and run on every open; register_migration callbacks use PRAGMA table_info, sqlite_master and a CHECK-rebuild of items (sqlite_sequence preserved); mirror widens its CHECK by editing sqlite_master SQL. None of this ports

Live holds 110 items (max id 113), 3,811 repo docs, 2,895 versions, 990 drafts, 7,855 + 61,932 vectors, 3,896 outbox rows, eval runs 1-71 and API keys 1-19, in a 419 MB library.db. sqlite_sequence is kept so purged ids are never reused

Backups use the SQLite online backup API into snapshots/<stamp>/library.db plus a sha-verified shared files tree and manifest.json; restore needs an empty target and re-verifies. The blob half stays; the database half is replaced

SECRET_SETTINGS maps env vars to grant secrets; _refuse_secrets rejects them in live.env; plan() runs up -d --no-deps library mcp, so a postgres service would never be started by restart. A PG password fits as a new grant secret; the DSN is built in-app so live.env never holds it

scope_entries.surface: tests/*/conftest.py (6 Store(tmp_path) fixtures); 19 files importing sqlite3; .github/workflows/tests.yml:32, publish.yml:29; culture.yaml gate
scope_entries.finding: 1,695 tests. Stores are built per area with Store(tmp_path/'data'); 19 test files use sqlite3 directly (83 sites), 10 read sqlite_master, 2 monkeypatch store._open. CI test jobs run pytest -n auto on ubuntu-latest, where a pgvector service container fits; the culture.yaml gate has no service

deploy.md's What runs, Backups, Restart, Upgrading across a schema change (sqlite3 and sqlite_sequence commands) and Rollback sections, every section of backup.md, and CLAUDE.md's 'SQLite WAL store' and items kind-CHECK notes all assume SQLite

Base dependencies must stay empty (asserted three times), so a Postgres driver can only live in an extra. No storage seam exists today: 68 functions take sqlite3.Connection. Keeping SQLite means building and testing two backends; dropping it means core/ needs the driver at runtime

Rollback today is a verified snapshot plus a tagged image (culture-library:0.19.7). culture-rules pushes every 15 minutes, so a one-shot cutover needs a short write freeze or a re-push after; a side-by-side period doubles the write paths

Today's ranking is FTS5 bm25 with title weight 5. Postgres core full text ranks by ts_rank/ts_rank_cd without IDF, so exact rankings move either way; a BM25 extension would stay closer but adds a non-core dependency to the database image
No Postgres image or driver is referenced anywhere yet; the library's core and routes are synchronous, which matches psycopg 3's sync API
